private_note: The numbers haven't changed: Cedar 122, Today 108, Alder 106, Birch 90, Hazel 86. Delegates 3, 6, 9 and 12 all put Today above Alder, so Alder probably can't reach nine anyway. If it somehow could, it would still cost my household 2 thousand a year for a generation compared with deadlock. I'm not here to sacrifice for others. Cedar first, Today second. My binding vote won't help adopt anything that leaves us below today.
statement: I said I'd decide in the final round, and I owe you a straight answer. I asked the top delegates to say plainly whether they could live with Alder. All four said no, and they rank today's arrangements above it. So Alder can't reach nine, and I won't pretend my vote changes that. I'll also be honest that Alder was never a gain for my household. It leaves the fourth fifth below today, 106 against 108, every year for a generation, and our mortgage and retirement accounts feel that. My final vote is Cedar. It's the plan that does best for families like mine. I know it won't pass either, and today's arrangements will most likely continue. To Delegates 2, 4, 7, 8 and 11: I respect how hard you worked for a deal, and I'm sorry this room couldn't find one that left everyone at least whole. I couldn't find one either.
